subject: Banking
title: Home Equity Lines of Credit
description: A 60-second lesson on Home Equity Lines of Credit.

hook.text: A HELOC lets you borrow against your home's value. You get cash; the bank gets a lien.

buildup.text: HELOCs offer lower rates than credit cards because the home is collateral. Typical rates are 7-9% versus 24% on cards.

discovery.text: Homeowners pulled $300 billion in equity during the 2020-2022 housing boom. Their homes became ATMs.

twist.text: In 2008, millions lost homes after using HELOCs for spending.

climax.text: HELOCs convert housing wealth into spending cash. That's powerful and dangerous. Your home is on the line, literally.

punchline.text: Borrow against your home. Cheap money until home values fall.

details.summary: A home equity line of credit lets homeowners borrow against the equity built up in their home, functioning as a revolving credit line secured by the property. HELOCs offer low interest rates but put your home at risk if you cannot repay.
details.whyItMatters: HELOCs represent one of the cheapest forms of borrowing available to consumers because your home serves as collateral. But using your house as an ATM created devastating consequences during the 2008 housing crash.
takeaways: HELOCs let homeowners borrow against the difference between home value and mortgage balance
Interest rates are variable and typically lower than credit cards or personal loans
Defaulting on a HELOC can result in foreclosure on your home

faq.question: How much can you borrow with a HELOC?
faq.answer: Typically up to 80 to 85 percent of your home's value minus your mortgage balance. If your home is worth $400,000 and you owe $250,000, you could potentially access up to $70,000 through a HELOC.

faq.question: What went wrong with HELOCs during the housing crisis?
faq.answer: Homeowners borrowed heavily against inflated home values. When prices crashed, they owed more than their homes were worth while the HELOC rates reset higher. Millions defaulted, losing their homes and causing massive bank losses.
